assessment_summary: The alternative proof attempts to construct S^\circ as an intersection of polars of half-spaces. On lines 0028-0032, it falsely claims that if y \in S^\circ, then y^Tx <= 1 for all x satisfying a single defining inequality a_i^T x <= b_i. This reverses the inclusion property of polar sets (since S \subseteq H_i implies S^\circ \supseteq H_i^\circ, not the other way around) and is logically invalid. (Additionally, the subsequent calculation of the maximum on line 0033 is also algebraically incorrect.)
